taxonomy_origin: TAXONOMY ORIGIN, WHICH IS A DIFFERENT FACT FROM THE DERIVATION ABOVE. The derivation line describes where FIELD CONTENT comes from: every field value traces to a standard, a regulation or a recognised industry body and carries its citation. It does NOT describe where the taxonomy comes from. Which processes exist, how they are grouped and what they are called is a practitioner synthesis of delivered implementations, generalised until it is product- and client-neutral. Of the 102 process groups, 43 originate in programme material, 28 in domain research, 20 in a published source and 11 in folder and file names; the provenance layer grades every one and names what to read next. This model is DELIVERED PRACTICE SPECIFIED AGAINST STANDARDS, not a standard turned into a model - and saying so is not a weakness. A taxonomy proven in delivery and then held against the standards is a stronger claim than one derived from a standard and never built.

processes.name: Evaluate and rank risk
processes.intent: Rank the identified threats so the programme can spend where it matters.
activities: Take each identified threat with its attribution and evidence
Evaluate likelihood and consequence on the adopted method
Return a rank for the threat against the system it reaches
Record the method and its uncertainty with the rank

trigger.text: Identified threats require evaluation and ranking.

outputs.what: Ranked threats with method and uncertainty
Ranking basis for the measures at 8.8.4

controls.text: 192.1007(c) requires the operator to evaluate the risks associated with the identified threats and to determine the relative importance of each. The section requires the evaluation and does not prescribe the method.

This ranks THREATS to the gas distribution system under a federal rule. 12.6.2 assesses an ASSET on the operator's own method, and it exists because not all asset risk assessment is regulatory - some is simply procedure. Both are kept. Ruled by Tim, 2026-08-30.
The method and its uncertainty are recorded with the rank. A rank carried forward without its method cannot be re-evaluated at 8.8.6, and re-evaluation is a required element.

measures.definition: Proportion of identified threats carrying a rank and a recorded method.

measures.name: Rank stability
measures.definition: Proportion of threats whose rank moved at the last re-evaluation.
measures.cite: SMRP Best Practices, Pillar 5 Work Management

variants: Ranking on a qualitative likelihood and consequence method
Ranking on a quantitative or scored method
Ranking where evidence is too thin to separate threats
Ranking of a threat identified from an unknown material or vintage

notation.why: A determination whose rule no source states. 192.1007(c) requires the evaluation and prescribes no method, so writing the DMN would mean inventing the ranking rule rather than citing it.

processes.name: Select and implement risk-reduction measures
processes.intent: Choose the measures that will reduce the ranked risk, and get them implemented.
activities: Take the ranked threats and the measures available against each
Select the measures the programme will implement
Release them as work, as procedure change or as replacement demand
Track implementation against what was selected

inputs.what: Measures available and their expected effect

controls.text: 192.1007(d) requires the operator to identify and implement measures to address the risks. Identification alone does not satisfy it; the implementation is part of the element.

A measure is tracked against the threat it was selected for, not against the work order that delivered it. Work completed that was never linked to a threat cannot be shown to have reduced the risk it was chosen for.
Where the measure is a replacement programme it enters 17.4's capital programme and competes there. The integrity rank is an input to that competition, not an authorisation to spend.

processes.name: Measure programme performance against baseline
processes.intent: Measure whether the programme is working, against what it was before.
activities: Take the programme's performance measures and their baseline
Collect the period's results from the operating record

controls.text: 192.1007(e) requires the operator to measure performance, monitor results and evaluate effectiveness. Measuring without evaluating whether the measures worked satisfies only part of the element.
Performance is judged against the baseline the programme set, not against last period. A measure that improved on last period while remaining worse than baseline is not working.

This process produces the results. 8.8.7 produces and validates the four measures that must be reported, and 15.3.1 files the report. Three processes, because producing, validating and submitting have different owners and different evidence.

processes.intent: Re-evaluate the whole programme on the cycle, and improve it where it fell short.
activities: Take the programme, its threats, ranks, measures and performance
Re-evaluate each element against what the period showed
Revise threats, ranks and measures where the evidence has moved
Reissue the programme and record what changed and why

inputs.what: New evidence since the last evaluation

outputs.what: Record of what changed and why

controls.text: 192.1007(f) requires the operator to periodically evaluate the programme and improve it. The cycle is set in Subpart P and the section is the authority for the figure; it is not restated here.
192.1013 requires a deviation from the programme to be reported. A re-evaluation that quietly changes what the programme requires, without recording the change, is how a deviation becomes invisible.
Re-evaluation revises the elements; it does not replace them. Carrying forward the previous threats, ranks and their methods is what makes the movement between cycles readable.

Re-evaluation following an incident or a deviation

processes.name: Report the four mandatory integrity measures
processes.intent: Produce the four measures the rule names, and prove each number is right.
activities: Take the four measures the rule requires and their definitions
Assemble the period's records against each definition
Reconcile the population and resolve exceptions before the number is fixed
Return the validated measures with the evidence behind them

trigger.text: The reporting period for the required integrity measures has closed.

inputs.what: Leak, damage, corrosion and excavation records

outputs.what: Four validated measures with their evidence

controls.text: 192.1007(e) and (g) require the operator to measure performance and to report the results, and 191.11 is the annual distribution report the measures are reported on. The four measures are named in the rule and are not the operator's to choose.

This process produces and validates the numbers. 15.3.1 files the report. Producing a number and submitting it are different processes with different owners and different evidence, and merging them is how an unreconciled number reaches a regulator. Ruled by Tim, 2026-08-30.
Reconciliation precedes the number. A measure calculated from an unreconciled population is a number the operator cannot defend, and the exception record is what makes it defensible.

processes.intent: Hold the written public-education programme the rule requires.

Write or revise the programme, its messages and its delivery plan
Approve and issue the programme version

inputs.what: System extent and the communities it reaches

controls.text: 192.616 requires a written continuing public education programme following the guidance in API RP 1162. The section sets no interval figure of its own; the delivery frequencies come from the RP.

API RP 1162 is guidance the section points to, not law in itself. It is recommended practice from a member-gated body, and where the programme departs from it the departure and its rationale are recorded.
Gas only. There is no electric distribution public awareness obligation of this kind, because 16 U.S.C. 824o places local distribution outside the federal regime.

processes.name: Identify stakeholder audiences
processes.intent: Establish who has to be reached, and where they are.
activities: Take the system extent and the areas it passes through
Identify the audiences the guidance names

inputs.what: Premise and contact data where held

controls.text: 192.616 requires the programme to reach the affected public, emergency officials, local public officials and excavators. Those four audiences come from the section and the guidance, not from the operator's preference.

The affected public is defined by proximity to the system, so the audience list is a spatial question before it is a marketing one. It is built from the network footprint, not from the customer list - a resident who is not a customer is still affected public.
An audience that cannot be reliably reached is recorded as such. It is an effectiveness finding for 8.9.4, not a gap to be quietly excluded from the population.

processes.intent: Deliver the messages to each audience at the frequency the guidance sets.
activities: Take the audience list and the message set for each

controls.text: 192.616 requires the programme to be carried out, not merely written. The delivery record is what shows it was, and a programme document with no delivery evidence satisfies nothing.

Baseline and supplemental messages are different obligations. Baseline runs on the cycle; supplemental is triggered by an event or an audience need, and delivering more baseline does not discharge a supplemental requirement.
Undeliverable contacts are a finding, not a rounding error. They reduce the coverage 8.9.4 measures and they are carried forward for the next audience identification.

processes.name: Measure effectiveness and retain records
processes.intent: Establish whether the messages landed, and keep what proves the programme ran.
activities: Take the delivery record and the audience population it aimed at
Measure reach, and comprehension where the guidance requires it
Evaluate effectiveness against the programme's objectives
Retain the evidence and return findings to the programme

trigger.text: A public awareness effectiveness evaluation is due.

inputs.what: Delivery record by audience and method

controls.text: 192.616 requires the effectiveness of the programme to be evaluated. Delivery volume is not effectiveness; the section asks whether the programme worked, and the guidance sets how that is judged.

Reach and comprehension are different measures and only one of them can be read off the delivery record. Comprehension requires asking the audience, and a programme that reports only reach has not evaluated effectiveness.
The retained evidence is what a regulator inspects. It runs to the message content, the audience list, the delivery record and the evaluation - not the evaluation alone.
